transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because people keep acting like I’m imagining things, but I’m not. For months there’ve been little things with money, mistakes showing up, and people looking at me differently at church. I know my husband’s family is behind it somehow, trying to hurt our name. Even when people show me records, it doesn’t change what’s really going on.

Besides these concerns about your husband's family, have you noticed any recent changes in your mood, like feeling unusually high, energetic, or irritable, or on the other hand, very sad or low, that lasted for days or weeks?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say high or anything like that. I get upset, sure, but that’s because of what’s been happening. I don’t think my mood is the issue.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people around you don't seem to hear or see?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I hear what anyone would hear. I haven’t seen things like that.

Aside from these concerns about your husband's family, how have things been going with your daily routine—like your job, taking care of the house, or spending time with friends? Have you noticed any changes there?

I still do what I need to do. I get up for work, do the billing stuff, keep the house in order. I garden some, paint when I feel like it.

It’s mostly a problem when I try to tell people what’s going on with my in-laws. That’s when things get… difficult.
How long have you been noticing and believing that your husband’s family is behind these issues with money and how people look at you?
About nine months, I guess. Since the problems with his family started… the money things, and the holidays. That’s when I began noticing it.

Have others told you that your speech or thoughts seem jumbled or hard to follow, or that your behavior has seemed unusual or disorganized in ways unrelated to this situation with your husband's family?
No… not really. I mean, people say I get upset or stuck on things, but I don’t think anyone’s said I’m jumbled or… disorganized like that. Not that I know of.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre delusional belief (that her husband's family is conspiring against her regarding finances and reputation) persisting for approximately 9 months. There is no evidence of hallucinations, disorganized speech, or disorganized/catatonic behavior. Mood symptoms (mania or depression) are denied and not prominent or sustained. Functioning outside the delusional theme remains largely intact (she continues to work, manage household tasks, and engage in hobbies), though social/interpersonal friction occurs when discussing the delusion. This clinical picture—an isolated, persistent delusion without other psychotic or mood symptoms and preserved functioning—is most consistent with Delusional Disorder (F22) rather than Schizophrenia (which requires broader psychotic symptoms or functional decline) or a mood disorder with psychotic features (which requires prominent mood episodes).
